messages:
anya (Finance): FYI nightly reconciliation flagged 23 potential duplicates. they look like late-arriving Stripe events that the backfill picked up as new invoices.

Tom (Revenue Ops): any pattern on customers or timestamps?

ria (Eng): quick look: Stripe event timestamps are older than delivery timestamps by 2-12 hours for this batch — Signed at 2025-12-02T03:xxZ, delivered at 2025-12-02T14:xxZ. webhook consumer treats delivery time as creation time when external_source_id missing, so backfill replayed them.

ben (SRE): ops-bot: pause cron billing-backfill
ops-bot: cronjob "billing-backfill" scaled to 0 (requested by ben).

ria (Eng): root cause: our queueing proxy (svc/event-relay) was under GC pressure and delayed delivery. proxy also strips stripe-event-time header in some retries. fix: 1) ensure header preserved on retries 2) add retry-delay metric and alert 3) backfill should check stripe_event_created_at before creating NS record.

anya (Finance): how many impacted? should AR handle manually?

ria (Eng): detection query: 23 NS invoices where external_source_id null and stripe_event_created_at < ns_created_at - 1h. 18 customers; 7 enterprise. recommend auto-void for non-enterprise under $300, manual review for enterprise.

Tom (Revenue Ops): starting auto-void for 16 invoices now. creating AR ticket for 7 enterprise ones.

ben (SRE): deployed proxy GC tweak and header-preserve patch. will run controlled replays for non-enterprise events after backfill paused.

ria (Eng): created ticket BILL-1107: backfill idempotency should prefer stripe_event_created_at if external_source_id missing.

anya (Finance): thanks. please tag me when the enterprise list is ready so AR can notify customers.

Tom (Revenue Ops): enterprise list sent to AR. monitoring for duplicates after controlled replay. so far no new dupes. :thumbsup:
